headings.text: ATAK connected to takserver - Point Dropper - Markers

blocks.html:
ATAK - Point Dropper - Basic use

ATAK connected to takserver - Point Dropper - Markers

slides.title: 1. Drawing Markers with Point Dropper
slides.html: • Tap the Point Dropper when you want to draw markers to the map.

slides.title: 2. Specify Marker Type
slides.html: • Tap "Ground" to specify your marker's subtype further if you so wish. You can edit this later too.

slides.title: 3. Select Marker Affiliation
slides.html: • Tap Unknown, Neutral, Enemy and Friendly for affiliation and to start dropping your new Marker.

slides.title: 4. Tap on map to drop the pointer
slides.html: • The pointer spawns upon tap. It is present only in your local device now - to share it, fill in some details and send it.

slides.title: 5. Select Marker for Editing or Send
slides.html: • Tap the marker to bring up the action menu. Tap the details icon, right next of the delete icon to fill details.

slides.title: 6. Open the Name dialog
slides.html: • Tap on the generated name of your marker in order to edit it.

slides.title: 7. Name your Marker
slides.html: • Name your marker according to your unit's convention. This example follows a scheme like so: "Reporting unit name, Descriptive Title"

slides.title: 8. Change Type
slides.html: • Tap Type to edit the marker subtype similarily as before.

slides.title: 9. Type Choices
slides.html: • There's plenty of choice for marker subtypes. Specify yours if applicable.

slides.title: 10. Set Location Error (Optional)
slides.html: • You can specify the location error of your symbol if applicable. It describes how accurate your marker's geolocation is.

slides.title: 11. Location Error Choices
slides.html: • As of NATO standard, you may specify the error from CAT1 (lowest) to CAT6 (highest error).

slides.title: 12. Specify Marker Size (Optional)
slides.html: • If your marker subtype is "Unit", you can specify the markers' size indication (eg. squad, platoon, company). Tap Unit Modifier/Echelon to do that.

slides.title: 13. From Squad to Army
slides.html: • Choose as applicable.

slides.title: 14. Fill in details using Remarks
slides.html: • Tell more about the marker by scrolling down and tapping the pen icon.

slides.title: 15. Fill in
slides.html: • Fill in details as needed.

slides.title: 16. Edit marker's Status
slides.html: • If applicable, you can alter the Status of this marker. This is usable if you edit an existing marker to reflect a change, or are planning anticipated action.

slides.title: 17. Edit spotting Sensors
slides.html: • If you happen to have sensor, eg. video stream, going on against the target, you can fill that by tapping the "play" icon.

slides.title: 18. Adding a video sensor to a marker
slides.html: • Stream using MediaMTX [separate guide] or via platform like YouTube in order to start the stream. You have to specify address, port, protocol and possible password though. This will be instructed in MediaMTX's guide.

slides.title: 19. Adding attachments
slides.html: • You can attachments eg. images to your marker. To do so, tap the pin icon.

slides.title: 20. Adding an attachment
slides.html: • You can eg. shoot a fresh image, or choose from your images using Image File.

slides.title: 21. Adding an image
slides.html: • Done adding attachments, go back to the main marker details screen via the back arrow.

slides.title: 22. Sending the point
slides.html: • Any marker you draw exists on your device only, unless you send the marker to somebody. We cover this further here.

slides.title: Done
slides.html: • You can close this guide.
